ai.description: This 30–40 cm snake is dark brown to black with iridescent scales. It features a blunt, shield-like tail ending in a sharp, keratinous spine and a small, pointed head. Family: Uropeltidae.
ai.identificationRemarks: Distinguish *Platyplectrurus madurensis* by its unique scale rows; it possesses 15 mid-body scale rows, whereas similar *Platyplectrurus* species typically have 17.
ai.habitat: The Travancore Hills Thorntail Snake inhabits high-altitude montane evergreen forests and shola grasslands in the Western Ghats, typically found above 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Travancore Hills Thorntail Snake is primarily nocturnal and fossorial, spending much of its time burrowing through leaf litter and soil in search of earthworms.
ai.reproductionNotes: The Travancore Hills Thorntail Snake is oviparous, laying a small clutch of eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Platyplectrurus madurensis* is endemic to the high-elevation shola forests and grasslands of the southern Western Ghats in Kerala and Tamil Nadu, India.
